draft.title: Economic agents and sectors
card: An economic agent is a decision-maker in the economy. There are three: consumers, businesses and government.
households that decide what goods and services to buy with their income.
organisations that decide what to produce, how to produce it and what to sell.

decides on laws, taxes and spending, and also provides some goods and services, such as public schools. The private sector is owned by individuals and firms. The public sector is owned and run by government.
draft.remember: Three agents make decisions. Who owns an organisation decides its sector.

a.q: Which of these is part of the public sector in Victoria?
opts: A café owned by Mia in Geelong
A bakery chain owned by shareholders
A family-owned plumbing firm in Bendigo
a.why: A state government school is owned and run by government, so it is in the public sector. The café, the bakery chain and the plumbing firm are owned by people or firms, so they are private, even though they serve the public.

b.q: Dev opens a gym in Ballarat and decides what classes to offer and what to charge. In which role is Dev making these decisions, and in which sector is the gym?
opts: A business owner, in the private sector
A business owner, in the public sector
A consumer, in the private sector
A government agent, in the public sector
b.why: Dev decides what to sell and at what price, which is what a business does. The gym is owned by an individual, not by government, so it is private. Serving the public does not make an organisation public sector.
b.clue: Decide the role by what is being decided, and the sector by who owns it.

b.best: A business owner, in the private sector
